c: Timothy

Timothy traveled with Paul for much of his missionary career and was one of Paul’s best-loved and most trusted assistants. Two of Paul’s last letters were written to Timothy at a time when Timothy was providing leadership for the church in Ephesus, near the end of Paul’s life.
Timothy had a devout mother and grandmother (

), and he was highly respected by the Christians in his hometown, Lystra, and in nearby Iconium. He joined Paul’s missionary team on Paul’s second missionary journey. Paul speaks of prophetic words that confirmed Timothy’s selection. Timothy also received a special gifting for service through the laying on of the hands of the elders and of Paul (
). Out of deference to the Jews in the area, Paul had Timothy circumcised (
Over the next fifteen years, Paul sent Timothy on special assignments to several different churches (
; see also
). Paul included Timothy’s name as coauthor of several of his letters (
). It is clear that Paul had a close relationship with Timothy and held him in high regard (see
). As Paul neared the end of his life and awaited his sentence in prison, he longed to see Timothy (
). Of all Paul’s coworkers, Timothy especially is commended for his selfless concern for Christ and his people (

In Paul’s second letter to Timothy (2 Timothy), written shortly before Paul was killed, he encouraged Timothy to be bold and fearless in his proclamation of the Good News, willing to suffer for Christ (
)—a strong word to one who might have been timid by nature (see
). Timothy himself seems to have become a prisoner later on (

Timothy was exemplary in the way he faithfully served the cause of Christ behind the scenes, devoting himself selflessly and with single-minded focus to the work of Christ and the people of Christ wherever help was needed. He serves as a reminder that believers should seek to become strong and effective witnesses for Christ.
